claims.head: Look for Montréal to find the slot
claims.body: Montréal’s shots are among the league’s most dangerous (1st of 32: one expected goal for every 14.5 unblocked shots). Carolina ranks 32nd at keeping opponents to the outside.

claims.body: Carolina ranks 6th of 32 on the power play (8.1 expected goals per 60); Montréal ranks 26th on the penalty kill.

claims.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
claims.body: Carolina’s hit score is 109 (7th of 32) and Montréal’s is 107 (10th). 100 is league average, after adjusting for each arena’s scorer.

notes.text: L. Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: J. Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 70% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 22 seconds at a time, against 63 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by N. Ehlers (10 of 13 changes).

MTL.head: Not an easy night for Montréal
MTL.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and Montréal has home ice. Montréal can pull it off if it gets to the dangerous areas.

CAR.head: Carolina has a lot going for it
CAR.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and Montréal has home ice. Montréal can make it interesting if it gets to the dangerous areas.
